Eric Burlison questions decades-long delay in UAP disclosure via social media posts
J. S. Song
Rep. Eric Burlison, a U.S. Congressman representing Missouri’s 7th district since 2023, posted a series of tweets on June 30, 2026, focusing on the topic of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (UAP) disclosure and its timeline.
In his first tweet at 16:55 UTC, Burlison stated, "Everyone wants UAP disclosure. Almost nobody asks why it's taken nearly 80 years. @ProfAviLoeb @haroldputhoff @UAPGERB Episode 73: https://t.co/yfgswuHPCc". The post referenced several figures in the field and linked to an episode for further discussion.
Later that day at 17:30 UTC, he followed up with another message: "@ProfAviLoeb @haroldputhoff @UAPGERB Watch the episode on YouTube here: https://t.co/yWTqXGiH69". This tweet provided direct access to the episode mentioned previously.
At 19:32 UTC, Burlison shared a third post containing only a link: "https://t.co/39WTlNcJnt".
Eric Burlison has served in Congress since replacing Billy Long in 2023 and previously held positions in both the Missouri House of Representatives from 2009 to 2017 and the Missouri Senate from 2019 to 2023. He was born in Springfield, Missouri, in 1976 and currently resides in Ozark. Burlison is an alumnus of Missouri State University, graduating with degrees earned in both 2000 and 2002.
